en.summary: Revenue was essentially flat YoY, but a larger gross-profit pool did not offset higher operating expenses. Cash flow recovered from the previous quarter while remaining well below year-ago FCF. Separate automotive, energy and service economics, and distinguish current reported profitability from the investment case for businesses still being scaled.
findings: Revenue was $28.046B, changing -0.174% YoY. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.22 versus $0.39 a year ago. These are realized standalone results for 2026-07-01–2026-09-30; changes in the business mix and special items need to be evaluated alongside the consolidated comparison.

GAAP operating income was $718M. Dividing it by revenue gives an operating margin of about 2.56%, versus 5.78% a year ago. The financial table separately retains GAAP gross margin of 19.589%. Gross and operating margins measure different expense levels; neither measures cash left after capital investment or the return earned on the installed asset base.

Quarterly OCF of $6.263B was close to $6.238B a year ago, while capex rose to $4.732B from $2.248B. FCF therefore fell to $1.531B from $3.990B. Sequentially, it improved from negative $1.092B in Q2 as cash investment fell. These comparisons show different baselines; neither proves that the long-term investment cycle has ended.

Gross profit rose from $5.054B to $5.494B, but operating expenses rose by $1.346B to $4.776B. The expense increase exceeded the $440M gross-profit improvement, explaining the fall in operating income from $1.624B to $718M. This is an operating-cost issue that a higher headline gross margin alone does not resolve.

GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders was $787M and diluted EPS $0.22, versus company-adjusted figures of $1.697B and $0.48. The adjustment gap is substantial relative to GAAP profit. Keep compensation and other reconciliation items visible when using adjusted results to assess earnings durability.

Automotive regulatory-credit revenue was $113M, with the filing disclosing a $475M reversal from a terminated contract. This is distinct from vehicle unit demand and selling prices. Management’s robotaxi/robotics expansion plans also require execution and capital; current-quarter automotive results alone do not verify their future profitability or deployment scale.

segments.name: Automotive revenue category
segments.text: Revenue was $20.560B, down from $21.205B a year ago. It includes sales, leasing and regulatory credits. This product revenue category differs from the broader reportable Automotive segment, which also includes Services and Other; the two scopes should not be combined.

segments.name: Energy generation and storage
segments.text: Revenue was $2.881B versus $3.415B a year ago. Related cost of revenue was $1.927B, implying roughly 33.1% gross margin. Quarterly recognized revenue need not move in step with storage deployments, because product mix and recognition timing also matter.

segments.name: Services and other revenue category
segments.text: Revenue increased to $4.605B from $3.475B. Cost of revenue of $3.871B implies roughly 15.9% gross margin. Faster sales growth here can coexist with a different margin profile from vehicle sales or storage products.

limitations: Analysis uses the listed official filings, releases and financial attachments; official call text has not been fully reviewed.
Product/geographic categories, reportable segments and adjusted measures retain their disclosed perimeters and must not be double-counted or substituted for consolidated GAAP results.
Cash flows are standalone; cumulative disclosures are differenced across adjacent periods. Issuer adjustments, leases and incentives are identified in metric definitions.
No pre-release consensus snapshot was preserved. Management guidance and analytical inferences are distinct from realized results.

metrics.label: GAAP gross margin
metrics.definition: GAAP gross profit divided by quarterly revenue.

metrics.label: Calculated free cash flow
metrics.definition: Standalone quarterly operating cash flow less cash capital purchases.
